## codegraph
# Codegraph — code intelligence over an indexed knowledge graph

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of every symbol, edge, and file in
the workspace — pre-computed structure you would otherwise re-derive by
reading files (cached intelligence: thousands of parse/trace decisions you
don't pay to re-reason each run). Reads are sub-millisecond; the index lags
writes by ~1s through the file watcher. Reach for it BEFORE *and* while
writing or editing code — not just for questions: one call returns the
verbatim source PLUS who calls it and what it affects, so you edit with the
blast radius in view. More accurate context, in far fewer tokens and
round-trips than reading files yourself.

## One tool: codegraph_explore — use it instead of reading files

There is a single tool, `codegraph_explore`, and it is Read-equivalent. It
takes either a natural-language question or a bag of symbol/file names and
returns the **verbatim, line-numbered source** of the relevant symbols
grouped by file — the same `<n>\t<line>` shape `Read` gives you, safe to
`Edit` from — PLUS the call path among them (including dynamic-dispatch hops
like callbacks, React re-render, and JSX children that grep can't follow) and
a blast-radius summary of what depends on them.

Whether you're answering "how does X work" or implementing a change (fixing a
bug, adding a feature), call `codegraph_explore` before you Read. ONE call
usually answers the whole question. Codegraph IS the pre-built search index —
so running your own grep + read loop, or delegating the lookup to a separate
file-reading sub-task/agent, repeats work codegraph already did and costs more
for the same answer. A direct codegraph answer is typically one to a few
calls; a grep/read exploration is dozens.

## How to query

- **Almost any question — "how does X work", architecture, a bug, "what/where is X", or surveying an area** → `codegraph_explore` with a natural-language question or the relevant names. ONE capped call returns the verbatim source grouped by file; most often the ONLY call y… [truncated]

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. 133	func (s *APIV1Service) GetAttachmentBlob(attachment *store.Attachment) ([]byte, error) {
134		// For local storage, read the file from the local disk.
135		if attachment.StorageType == storepb.AttachmentStorageType_LOCAL {
136			attachmentPath := filepath.FromSlash(attachment.Reference)
137			if !filepath.IsAbs(attachmentPath) {
138				attachmentPath = filepath.Join(s.Profile.Data, attachmentPath)
139			}

141			file, err := os.Open(attachmentPath)
142			if err != nil {
143				if os.IsNotExist(err) {
144					return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "file not found")
145				}
146				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to open the file")
147			}
148			defer file.Close()
149			blob, err := io.ReadAll(file)
150			if err != nil {
151				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read the file")
152			}
153			return blob, nil
154		}
155		// For S3 storage, download the file from S3.
156		if attachment.StorageType == storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3 {
157			if attachment.Payload == nil {
158				return nil, errors.New("attachment payload is missing")
159			}
160			s3Object := attachment.Payload.GetS3Object()
161			if s3Object == nil {
162				return nil, errors.New("S3 object payload is missing")
163			}
164			if s3Object.S3Config == nil {
165				return nil, errors.New("S3 config is missing")
166			}
167			if s3Object.Key == "" {
168				return nil, errors.New("S3 object key is missing")
169			}
170	
171			s3Client, err := s3.NewClient(context.Background(), s3Object.S3Config)
172			if err != nil {
173				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create S3 client")
174			}
175	
176			blob, err := s3Client.GetObject(context.Background(), s3Object.Key)
177			if err != nil {
178				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get object from S3")
179			}
180			return blob, nil
181		}
182		// For database storage, return the blob from the database.
183		return attachment.Blob, nil
184	}

186	var fileKeyPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`\{[a-z]{1,9}\}`)

188	func replaceFilenameWithPathTemplate(path, filename string) string {
189		t := time.Now()
190		path = fileKeyPattern.ReplaceAllStringFunc(path, func(s string) string {
191			switch s {
192			case "{filename}":
193				return filename
194			case "{timestamp}":
195				return fmt.Sprintf("%d", t.Unix())
196			case "{year}":
197				return fmt.Sprintf("%d", t.Year())
198			case "{month}":
199				return fmt.Sprintf("%02d", t.Month())
200			case "{day}":
201				return fmt.Sprintf("%02d", t.Day())
202			case "{hour}":
203				return fmt.Sprintf("%02d", t.Hour())
204			case "{minute}":
205				return fmt.Sprintf("%02d", t.Minute())
206			case "{second}":
207				return fmt.Sprintf("%02d", t.Second())
208			case "{uuid}":
209				return util.GenUUID()
210			default:
211				return s
212			}
213		})
214		return path
215	}

217	func ensureUniqueLocalAttachmentPath(path, uid string) string {
218		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil {
219			return path
220		}
221	
222		ext := filepath.Ext(path)
223		base := strings.TrimSuffix(path, ext)
224		return base + "_" + uid + ext
225	}
226	
227	func validateFilename(filename string) bool {
228		// Reject path traversal attempts and make sure no additional directories are created
229		if !filepath.IsLocal(filename) || strings.ContainsAny(filename, "/\\") {
230			return false
231		}
232	
233		// Reject filenames starting or ending with spaces or periods
234		if strings.HasPrefix(filename, " ") || strings.HasSuffix(filename, " ") ||
235			strings.HasPrefix(filename, ".") || strings.HasSuffix(filename, ".") {
236			return false
237		}
238	
239		return true
240	}
241	
242	func normalizeMimeType(mimeType string) (string, bool) {
243		mimeType = strings.TrimSpace(mimeType)
244		if mimeType == "" || len(mimeType) > 255 {
245			return "", false
246		}
247	
248		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(mimeType)
249		if err != nil || mediaType == "" || len(mediaType) > 255 {
250			return "", false
251		}
252	
253		return mediaType, true
254	}

The **S3 presign runner** (`server/runner/s3presign`) keeps external attachment links fresh. Attachments stored in S3 are referenced by presigned URLs that expire after 5 days; this runner re-signs them before they go stale.

content.text:
h02.

**Outbound delivery** executes in `Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (specifically the actual HTTP send at `safeClient.Do(req)`, `internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`). Webhooks are enqueued via `PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`) and dispatched by the background worker goroutines started in `init` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42`), each of which calls `Post`.

**Protection against internal/private addresses:** the shared `safeClient` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32`) is configured with a custom transport whose `DialContext` is `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:59`). At dial time `safeDialContext` resolves the target host and rejects the connection if any resolved IP is a reserved/private address via `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:71`) — this also defeats DNS-rebinding since the check happens on the actual dialed IPs.

Answer: `Post` (with the send at `safeClient.Do`) — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (line 152); `safeDialContext` guarding the `safeClient` transport, rejecting reserved IPs via `isReservedIP` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:59` (check at line 71).

h05.

**Mechanism: explicit Go code** — a deleted user's emoji reactions are removed by an explicit SQL statement issued from Go inside the delete-user transaction, in each of the three DB drivers. (There is no DB-level cascade doing this; the code deletes reactions explicitly.)

What I checked:
- The store-facing entry `Store.DeleteUser` (`store/user.go:171`) delegates to the driver's `DeleteUser`. The API handler `APIV1Service.DeleteUser` (`server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:393`) calls it but does nothing with reactions itself.
- Each driver's `DeleteUser` runs `deleteUserTargetsTx` in a transaction (`store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:43`, `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:43`, `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:43`).
- Inside `deleteUserTargetsTx`, reactions are deleted by two explicit calls:
  - `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx(ctx, tx, contentIDs)` — reactions attached to the user's own memos (line 96 in all three: `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96`, `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96`, `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96`).
  - `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx(ctx, tx, userID)` — the reactions **the user authored** (their emoji reactions on any memo), at line 102 in all three drivers (`store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:102`, `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:102`, `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:102`).

So the user's emoji reactions are removed by explicit Go code (the `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` call), not by a database cascade rule and not left in place.

Answer: explicit Go code; `store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}/user_delete.go:102` (`deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`, the user's authored reactions) and `:96` (`deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`, reactions on the user's memos), both invoked from `deleteUserTargetsTx` (`:92`) within the transactional `DeleteUser` (`:29`), reached via `store/user.go:171`.

h07.

The browser hits `GET /file/users/{identifier}/avatar` (the URL the API hands back as `/file/{user}/avatar`, `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36`). The avatar image bytes live in the user row's `avatar_url` column as a base64 data URI, not on disk. Hops:

Route registration: `fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar)` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124
serveUserAvatar (serving handler) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168
getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
Store.GetUser — store/user.go:148
Store.ListUsers — store/user.go:136
driver.ListUsers (interface) — store/driver.go
DB.ListUsers (concrete SQL, selects `avatar_url`) — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (SELECT at :152–159; likewise store/db/postgres/user.go and store/db/mysql/user.go)

Then back in the handler the stored data URI (`user.AvatarURL`) is decoded and written to the response: `parseDataURI` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737, followed by `c.Blob(...)` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:209.

181			// Fenced code block with language
182			r.buf.WriteString("```")
183			if lang := fenced.Language(source); len(lang) > 0 {
184				r.buf.Write(lang)
185			}
186			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')

189			lines := fenced.Lines()
190			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
191				line := lines.At(i)
192				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))

198			}
199		} else if codeBlock, ok := node.(*gast.CodeBlock); ok {
200			// Indented code block
201			lines := codeBlock.Lines()
202			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
203				line := lines.At(i)
204				r.buf.WriteString("    ")
205				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
206			}
207			if node.NextSibling() != nil {

216		tempBuf := &bytes.Buffer{}
217		tempRenderer := &MarkdownRenderer{buf: tempBuf}
218		tempRenderer.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
219	
220		// Add "> " prefix to each line
221		content := tempBuf.String()
222		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(content, "\n"), "\n")
223		for i, line := range lines {
224			r.buf.WriteString("> ")
225			r.buf.WriteString(line)
226			if i < len(lines)-1 {
227				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
228			}
229		}

233	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderListItem(node *gast.ListItem, source []byte, depth int) {
234		parent := node.Parent()
235		list, ok := parent.(*gast.List)
236		if !ok {
237			r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
238			return
239		}
240	
241		// Add indentation only for nested lists
242		// Document=0, List=1, ListItem=2 (no indent), nested ListItem=3+ (indent)
243		if depth > 2 {
244			indent := strings.Repeat("  ", depth-2)
245			r.buf.WriteString(indent)
246		}
247	
248		// Add list marker
249		if list.IsOrdered() {
250			fmt.Fprintf(r.buf, "%d. ", list.Start)
251			list.Start++ // Increment for next item
252		} else {
253			r.buf.WriteString("- ")
254		}
255	
256		// Render content
257		r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
258	
259		// Add newline if there's a next sibling
260		if node.NextSibling() != nil {
261			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
262		}
263	}

The derived metadata is the memo's **`Payload`** — specifically `MemoPayload.Tags` and the computed `MemoPayload.Property` (`proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go:85`), which back list/preview features. It is computed from the memo content, not set by the user.

**Computation site:** `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`. It calls the markdown service's single-pass `ExtractAll` (interface `internal/markdown/markdown.go:33`, impl `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`) and writes the results onto the memo: `memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property = data.Property` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:85-86`).

**Triggers (recomputation):**
- **Create** — `CreateMemo` calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService)` before insert — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`.
- **Update (content change)** — `UpdateMemo` rebuilds the payload only when the `content` field is in the update mask — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447` (inside the `path == "content"` branch, `:436-451`).
- (The batch backfill method `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce`, `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27`, would also recompute for all memos, but it is dead code — never instantiated in production.)

**What the computation extracts** (`ExtractAll`, `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356-422`, persisted into the payload):
- **Tags** — every `#tag` node (excluding tags inside links/images), deduplicated preserving case (`data.Tags`).
- **Property** (`MemoPayload_Property`, fields at `proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go:85-92`):
  - `HasLink` — content contains a link (`markdown.go:393`).
  - `HasCode` — content contains a code block, fenced code block, or inline code span (`:396`).
  - `HasTaskList` — content contains a task checkbox (`:399`).
  - `HasIncompleteTasks` — content has at least one unchecked task checkbox (`:401-404`).
  - `Title` — text of the first-block H1 heading, if the document begins with one (`:384-388`).

(`ExtractAll` also collects `Mentions`, but those are consumed separately for mention notifications — `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32` — and are not stored in the persisted payload by `RebuildMemoPayload`.)

Answer: computation site = `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`, via `markdown.ExtractAll` `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`); triggers = `CreateMemo` (`memo_service.go:108`) and `UpdateMemo` when `content` changes (`memo_service.go:447`); extracted = deduped `#tags` plus the `Property` set `{HasLink, HasCode, HasTaskList, HasIncompleteTasks, Title(first H1)}`.

h15.

Memo view-access is enforced across several distinct server surfaces. Each distinct enforcement site:

- API v1 single-memo read gate (`checkMemoReadAccess`, used by `GetMemo`) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:38` (visibility checks at :55–:66; archived-only-to-creator at :44–:53)
- API v1 list query visibility filter (`ListMemos` restricts by current user) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:217`–`:227`, enforced in the SQL `WHERE` via `FindMemo.VisibilityList` — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:96` (and `store/db/postgres/memo.go`, `store/db/mysql/memo.go`)
- HTTP file server attachment/blob permission (`checkAttachmentPermission`) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:650` (visibility checks at :677 and :699)
- API v1 attachment service access check — `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:445`–`:451` and `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:214`–`:222`
- API v1 reaction service access check — `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30`–`:38` and `:83`
- API v1 memo comment access check — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41`
- RSS feed (public-only memos) — `server/router/rss/rss.go:90` and `:141`
- Frontend SSR / sitemap (public-only memos) — `server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150`

**Premise correction:** There is no Redis anywhere in this codebase. A repository-wide search for `redis` (case-insensitive, all `.go` files) returns zero matches. The cache layer is a **process-local, in-memory** cache — not backed by Redis or any external store — so there is no "Redis connection" to configure.

**Actual mechanism:**

content.text:
r02.

**Premise correction:** The premise is false — there is **no per-user (or any) API rate-limiting middleware in this codebase**, so there is no registration site and no request limits to report.

Evidence:
- A repository-wide search for rate-limiting constructs (`ratelimit`, `RateLimiter`, `limiter`, `throttle`, `golang.org/x/time/rate`, "requests per", "per second/minute") across all `.go` files returns **no matches**. Notably, Echo's `middleware.RateLimiter` is not used.
- The Echo middleware chain registers only `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware — `server/server.go:51`–`:52` (CORS defined in `server/cors.go:14`). No rate limiter is added.
- The API v1 request pipeline uses interceptors for metadata, logging, recovery, and **auth/authorization** only — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133`–`:137` (`NewMetadataInterceptor`, `NewLoggingInterceptor`, `NewRecoveryInterceptor`, `NewAuthInterceptor`); the gRPC-Gateway and Connect handlers share one `Authorizer` (`server/router/api/v1/authz.go`, `acl_config.go`). None of these throttle by user or rate.
- The only request "limits" present are unrelated size caps, not rate limits: a max request body size `maxAPIRequestBytes = 256 << 20` (256 MiB) enforced via `http.MaxBytesHandler` / `connect.WithReadMaxBytes` — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:20`, `:126`, `:141`, `:144` — and pagination page-size caps (`MaxPageSize`, `server/router/api/v1/common.go:16`).

So: the correct statement is that memos does not implement per-user API rate limiting; access is gated by authentication/authorization interceptors and by request-size/page-size caps, not by request-rate limits.

r03.

**Premise correction:** There is no nightly database-cleanup job — and in fact no job of any kind is scheduled through the cron scheduler. The premise is false on two counts.

Details / evidence:
- A cron scheduler package does exist (`internal/scheduler/` — `scheduler.go`, `parser.go`, `job.go`, supporting standard cron expressions), but it is **never instantiated or used in production**. Searching all non-test `.go` files for `scheduler.New`, `.Register(`, `.Start(` on the scheduler, or any `internal/scheduler` usage outside the package itself returns **no matches** — the package is only exercised by its own tests (`internal/scheduler/*_test.go`). So nothing is registered with the cron scheduler at all, let alone a database-cleanup job.
- There is no "database-cleanup" job anywhere. A search for `cleanup`/`nightly`/`purge`/`vacuum` finds only unrelated things: per-request attachment/relation cleanup during memo/user deletion (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:579`, `server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:421`+), and the **in-memory cache** eviction loop.
- The only actual background/periodic work the server runs (wired in `server/server.go` `startBackgroundRunners`) is:
  - the S3 presign runner, on a fixed 12-hour ticker (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`) — not cron, not nightly, not DB cleanup; and

r04.

**Premise correction:** Neither. The webhook delivery workers do not consume from any external message broker — there is no NATS, no RabbitMQ (nor AMQP/Kafka) anywhere in the codebase. A search for `nats`, `rabbitmq`, `amqp`, `streadway`, `kafka` across all `.go` files returns **no matches**, and there is no external queue declared.

**Actual mechanism:** delivery is dispatched through an **in-process, bounded Go channel** local to the `internal/webhook` package:
- The "queue" is a buffered channel `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:39` (capacity 128, in-memory, lost on restart).
- A fixed pool of **4 worker goroutines** is started in `init()` and each ranges over that channel, calling `Post` for every payload — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:42`–`:55` (`for range 4 { go func() { for payload := range asyncPostQueue { Post(payload) } }() }`).
- Producers enqueue non-blockingly via `PostAsync`, which does a `select` send onto the channel and **drops** the payload (with a warning log) if the buffer is full — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`–`:195` (send at `:190`). Callers such as `DispatchMemoCreated/Updated/Deleted/CommentCreatedWebhook` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`) feed it.

So the correct answer is: no broker at all — webhook workers consume from an in-memory buffered channel (`asyncPostQueue`) declared at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`, serviced by 4 goroutines started in `internal/webhook/webhook.go:42`.

**Premise correction:** There is no GraphQL API — and therefore no GraphQL schema — anywhere in this repository. Searching all `.go` files for `graphql`/`gqlgen` and searching for `*.graphql`/`*.graphqls` schema files both return **no matches**. The public API is not GraphQL.

**Actual API surface:** the public API is defined as **Protocol Buffers / gRPC**, exposed over REST (gRPC-Gateway) and Connect:
- The schema/service contracts live in `.proto` files under `proto/api/v1/` — e.g. `proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, plus `common.proto` (with HTTP/REST annotations via `google.api.http`).
- These generate Go stubs under `proto/gen/api/v1/` (`*.pb.go`, gRPC `*_grpc.pb.go`, gateway `*.pb.gw.go`, and Connect `apiv1connect/*.connect.go`).
- At runtime the services are registered in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (gRPC-Gateway mux + Connect handlers/interceptors, e.g. `v1.go:95`, `:133`–`:141`) and wired into the HTTP server via `apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(...)` in `server/server.go:88`. There is also an MCP surface (`server/router/mcp/`) and an RSS feed (`server/router/rss/`), but no GraphQL endpoint.

So: the correct location to look for the "public API schema" is the protobuf definitions in `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (served as gRPC/REST/Connect), not a GraphQL schema.
